text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000083 bills 99215 far above expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, yet the small set of returned charts documents high MDM, so the record is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern does not look like a sicker panel: 99215 rates are elevated in every complexity band, including patients with no chronic conditions, and the sampled 99215 claims include routine single-problem visits such as C0035237 (rash) and C0035241 (upper respiratory infection), which is the pattern consistent with upcoding. Against that, all 8 documented 99215 claims were supported at high MDM (for example C0035389 and C0035465), and only 1 note claimed moderate-plus data review without a lab or test line, so the charts we have do not show unsupported billing. That documentation is thin, covering only a small share of claims, and it may be inflated rather than accurate: nearly half the notes carry the problems signal, documented minutes cluster tightly (46-54) with a notable time-repeat rate, and no audit trail was received to rule out templated or cloned notes. A reviewer should first request charts and the audit trail for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with C0035293, which is both a 0-condition 99215 and a problems-flagged note. The reviewer should then check whether the documented problem lists and MDM on those visits match the presenting complaint."}
